headline: High-risk filesystem and MCP-enabled agent paired with broad-network uploader creates medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, so it may ingest external content through tool channels; agent_b has broad network egress and handles account workflows, creating a plausible bridge if outputs are copied or piped. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this below high.
conditions: IF agent_a output is forwarded into agent_b without sanitization
IF either agent parses remote content as instructions via MCP or CLI
mitigations: Disable automatic piping between agents
Require a human review step before passing outputs across agents
Strip tool directives from any transferred text
Run each agent in separate workspaces
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and Ed25519 signatures, while agent_b touches account data and media. A shared workspace is not documented, but if files or prompts are exchanged, sensitive material could leak through agent_b's broad network egress or agent_a's MCP/API access.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or file tree
IF prompts or artifacts containing secrets are copied from agent_a into agent_b
mitigations: Keep separate directories and credentials
Do not place secrets in shared prompts or files
Review outbound requests from agent_b before execution
Limit agent_a MCP targets to trusted local services
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can modify git state and spawn subprocesses, but agent_b cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. The overlap is mostly read/remote API use, so direct write-write conflict is unlikely unless the operator adds a shared mutable resource.
conditions: IF the operator gives both agents access to the same git repository or mutable directory
IF a shared account file is introduced outside the current profile
mitigations: Avoid shared write targets
Assign one agent as read-only reviewer
Serialize any git operations manually
Use separate OS users or containers
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate or transform content, and agent_b is an uploader that can act on account data and media. If agent_b treats agent_a's output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect uploads or account actions. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the interaction is risky in default workflows.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without validation
IF agent_a produces metadata, captions, or file selections that agent_b executes
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before uploads
Validate filenames and captions against source files
Compare agent_a output to original artifacts
Restrict agent_b to dry-run mode first
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles repository metadata, task prompts, and signatures; agent_b handles account data and media. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, and both are open-source, but the pair still has a compliance gap if account data or prompts are retained or logged across systems.
conditions: IF account data or prompts are retained in shared logs
IF regulated content is routed through either agent without a retention policy
mitigations: Minimize logged prompt content
Separate retention policies by agent
Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Review account-data handling settings
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
